newsitem.title: USA: No new aid seen until N. Korea replies on peace.
newsitem.headline: No new aid seen until N. Korea replies on peace.

text.p: Despite Pyongyang's demands, no new food aid pledges are expected until North Korea responds conclusively to a Korean peninsula peace talks proposal, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

They told Reuters North Korea began Wednesday's crucial meeting in New York by accepting a U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party peace talks but then conditioned that position with new demands for international assistance to meet severe food shortages.
As a result, "we don't have a deal," one official said.

Another official said the United States worked hard to avoid being put in a position where food aid was seen as a reward for North Korea's acceptance of the peace talks proposal. Washington sped normal bureaucratic procedures to announce an extra $15 million in assistance last Monday.
Asked if he expected the United States or South Korea to announce additional food aid before talks resume in New York on Friday, he said: "No, I don't."

"My expectation is that sooner or later the North Koreans are going to feel they accomplished their first priority: They sensitized the outside world to their needs and its being handled as much as it can be and they will turn to the question of peace talks and give a response. I'm still expecting that response will be favourable," he said.
